sentence: Not until the audit was complete did the extent of the red tape become apparent
hint: Inversion after 'Not until': Not until + clause + auxiliary + subject
explanation: 'Red tape' significa burocracia excesiva. 'Not until' provoca inversión en la cláusula principal.

sentence: The researcher had to move the goalposts when the initial hypothesis proved untenable
explanation: 'Move the goalposts' significa cambiar las reglas de forma injusta. 'Had to' se usa para necesidad en el pasado.

sentence: Were the government to turn a blind eye to corruption the consequences would be dire
hint: Formal conditional: Were + subject + to + base form
explanation: 'Turn a blind eye' significa ignorar algo deliberadamente. 'Were...to' es una forma condicional formal.

sentence: Rarely does a single policy shift the balance of power so dramatically
explanation: 'Shift the balance of power' significa cambiar quién tiene el control. 'Rarely' provoca inversión.

sentence: The whistleblower opened a Pandora's box that the board had tried to keep shut
explanation: 'Open a Pandora's box' significa desatar problemas imprevistos. Se usa el pasado perfecto para la acción anterior.

sentence: Under no circumstances should the team rest on their laurels after this success
explanation: 'Rest on one's laurels' significa volverse complaciente después de un éxito. Una frase negativa provoca inversión.

sentence: Had the negotiators not played hardball the deal would have fallen through
explanation: 'Play hardball' significa negociar de forma agresiva. 'Fall through' significa fracasar. Condicional invertida.

sentence: The professor suggested that we not take the findings at face value
hint: Subjunctive: suggested that + subject + base form
explanation: 'Take at face value' significa aceptar algo sin cuestionarlo. Se usa el subjuntivo después de 'suggested that'.

sentence: Only after the merger did the company gain the upper hand in the market
explanation: 'Gain the upper hand' significa obtener una ventaja. 'Only after' provoca inversión.

sentence: It is imperative that the board not sweep these allegations under the carpet
hint: Subjunctive: It is imperative that + subject + base form
explanation: 'Sweep under the carpet' significa ocultar un problema. Se usa el subjuntivo después de 'it is imperative that'.

sentence: The new legislation cuts both ways for small businesses
explanation: 'Cut both ways' significa tener efectos tanto positivos como negativos.

sentence: After decades in exile the policy debate has come full circle
explanation: 'Come full circle' significa volver a una posición o situación original después de un período de cambios.

sentence: The ruling could set a dangerous precedent for future cases
explanation: 'Set a precedent' significa establecer un ejemplo o modelo que las futuras decisiones seguirán.

sentence: The lawyer's objection only served to muddy the waters
explanation: 'Muddy the waters' significa hacer que una situación sea más confusa o poco clara.

sentence: New evidence could tip the scales in favor of the defense
explanation: 'Tip the scales' significa ser el factor decisivo en una situación.
